% brando's dogfood of brand_doc — the rule that had no in-repo caller.
%
% brando 0.2.0 renamed the LaTeX macros off fastverk's `fv` prefix
% (\fvswatch -> \brandswatch, \fvheader -> \brandheader) and every colour name
% with them. Nothing in this repo compiled a .tex, so the rename passed every
% test here and broke fastverk/brand's CI instead, with
% `onepager.tex:5: Undefined control sequence`.
%
% The lesson is narrow and worth stating: rendering a template proves the template
% RENDERS. It says nothing about whether the macros it defines still have the
% names their callers use. Only compiling a document that calls them proves that.
%
% So this document calls every macro the brand class defines. Rename one again and
% this fails here, in brando, rather than in a consumer's CI a week later.
\documentclass{brandofixture}
\begin{document}

\section{Colour}
\brandswatch{brandbg}{18181B}\quad
\brandswatch{brandfg}{FAFAFA}\quad
\brandswatch{brandaccent}{D4D4D8}\quad
\brandswatch{brandmuted}{A1A1AA}

\section{Text}
Body text set in the brand's main font, so the \verb|\setmainfont| path is
exercised rather than merely templated.

\end{document}
